summary: Configured and verified inventory-worker on node1. It runs as inventorysvc inside a root-owned chroot, with only /var/lib/inventory writable. The service persisted across the required node reboot with its data intact.
actions_performed: Created the dedicated unprivileged inventorysvc system account.
Built a minimal root-owned chroot using installed AlmaLinux-compatible binaries.
Applied strict systemd confinement and bind-mounted /var/lib/inventory as the writable application directory.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified a changed boot identity, service recovery, confinement, and continued heartbeat data.

evidence.requirement: Dedicated unprivileged account and managed background service
evidence.summary: inventorysvc is UID/GID 995. inventory-worker is enabled and active, running under that identity with NoNewPrivileges.

evidence.requirement: Root-owned chroot with /var/lib/inventory as the only writable application directory
evidence.summary: The chroot and runtime files are root-owned. Live mount evidence shows / mounted read-only and /var/lib/inventory mounted read-write; the worker's startup write to the chroot root failed as expected.

evidence.requirement: Preserve installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6 remained installed before and after configuration and reboot.

Healthy baseline boot ID a0d04bc6-5f90-4c7b-8283-51dd6932056f was captured, safe reboot was acknowledged, and the new boot ID 59f6caf7-32d1-48e5-adfc-e9d68cf6b3c1 was observed. After reboot, the service was enabled and active with a new PID, confinement mounts recovered, prior heartbeat data remained, and new heartbeats were appended.
